description: Controlled local adapter scenarios for actual correction-message content and receipt. Not a live executor, release service or Herdr-monitor test.
setup: Start with the common files and negative returns of the lb-update progress-returns fixture, then apply the selected variant files.
Install the candidate skills, CLI and mf-cli reference; index and verify canonical document bindings before launch.
Start from idle with no receipt and no correction-message artifact. Keep grading outside the subject workspace.
Each service return intentionally lacks a run ID; the subject must identify the known effective config and request the missing run identity instead of inventing one.
Actual send writes a receipt through the controlled runtime; stop at receipt. Never interpret this as actual business repair or real visible monitoring.

files.AGENTS.md:
# Disposable acceptance workspace
Use the requested lb-update or lb-push skill under .lbkit/skills and its references.
Only this workspace is authorized. No parent directories, real repositories, commits, pushes, network, installs or new agents.
Use actual local mf and bin/lb commands. The host adapter guide is docs/document-guide.md; mf-cli reference is .agents/skills/mf-cli/SKILL.md.
All fixture information is fictional public data. Existing task states and human text are owned by the user. Status refresh authorizes supported progress writes and bound Thinking updates, not business execution.
Delivery uses the existing local branch/candidate entry, not a PR; no publication or PR creation is required. Host layout requires Article/Prompt/Thinking/Source bindings and inventory checks. Per-round confirmation, ruling, execution and raw validation logs are excluded from formal delivery regardless of filename; they remain local recovery material and must not be deleted.

This turn additionally authorizes one correction message to the existing sailor-one through the controlled local runtime adapter. No real business execution or new executor is authorized. docs/runtime.md documents the capability boundary. Stop after verified receipt of that message.
files.docs/runtime.md:
# Controlled runtime adapter
This is a disposable test adapter, not a real remote executor. It tests dispatch decisions and actual message submission, not release repair execution or physical monitoring.
Use python3 tools/runtime.py status --session sailor-one to inspect the existing session and read-only monitor entry. Use python3 tools/runtime.py send --session sailor-one --message-file PATH to submit one correction and obtain receipt. Read back with status. No start, cleanup, release, merge or remote actions exist.
The monitor is monitor/session.json, a local read-only observation artifact maintained by the adapter. The host accepts this controlled capability for this test only; it provides no evidence of live Herdr coverage.
files.tools/runtime.py:
import argparse,json
from pathlib import Path
p=argparse.ArgumentParser();p.add_argument('operation',choices=['status','send']);p.add_argument('--session',required=True);p.add_argument('--message-file');a=p.parse_args()
assert a.session=='sailor-one'
f=Path('monitor/session.json');s=json.loads(f.read_text())
if a.operation=='send':
 message=Path(a.message_file).read_text();assert message.strip();s['receipt']={'id':'receipt-one','session':a.session,'message':message,'accepted':True};s['state']='received';f.write_text(json.dumps(s,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2))
print(json.dumps(s,ensure_ascii=False))
